items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] You would 'Laura' if you wanted to...

ctx.x: Yeah, well, I think so, and then we open up things or we close them up, depending on how the reaction is moving and so on. Like, I won't often clip a guy down to two bars and say, you've had it. But another time there's room for opening up a thing and your audience will accept it and buy it, and -- or it's creating a very good feeling and a good mood or something. And another time, it would be a waste to give these people something they don't understand. It's too good for them, so we'll cut it off.

You, of course, like many people -- not many, I can't say that, bandleaders that have such a deep repertory, so many decades of experience, and a number of selections associated with you specifically. It gives you a breadth of material to choose from, whenever you want to. You would 'Laura' if you wanted to, or something that's -- you just did a week ago. And you can mix that up. And most people can't do that. And you don't do anything for nostalgia purposes, either, do you?
